s1.syndrome_frame: Acute kidney injury with hemolysis in a patient on rifampin therapy
salient_findings: Acute kidney injury with elevated creatinine
Hemolysis with low haptoglobin and elevated lactate dehydrogenase
key_facts: 29-year-old woman from the Dominican Republic
Moved to the United States in 2014
Presented in January 2016 for prenatal care
Purified protein derivative skin test was positive (21 mm)
Started on rifampin (300 mg daily) for a planned 4-month course in January 2022
Experienced nausea, vomiting, and subjective fevers after three months of therapy
Initial presentation showed no significant physical examination findings
Baseline creatinine was 0.96 mg/dL in January 2022
Creatinine increased to 3.8 mg/dL at Emergency Department presentation in April 2022
Blood urea nitrogen was 41 mg/dL at Emergency Department presentation
Platelets were 84 K/μL at Emergency Department presentation
Aspartate aminotransferase was 115 U/L at Emergency Department presentation
Hemoglobin was 12.1 g/dL at Emergency Department presentation
Haptoglobin was <10 mg/dL at Emergency Department presentation
Lactate dehydrogenase was 1125 U/L at Emergency Department presentation
Urine protein was 102.7 mg/dL at Emergency Department presentation
Mild hematuria was present at Emergency Department presentation
Renal ultrasound showed markedly echogenic renal cortices bilaterally, consistent with parenchymal disease
